BASE_TRAIN_SENTENCE: Training loss fell from 1.897 to 1.033, rising in only 2 of 29 epoch-to-epoch steps, and training accuracy climbed to 62.77%.
BASE_ACC_SENTENCE: Validation accuracy behaved differently: it peaked at 48.68% in epoch 21 and finished at 45.76%, so the 9 epochs after the peak bought nothing on unseen data.
BASE_TREND_SENTENCE: Validation loss reached its minimum of 1.494 at epoch 11 and then climbed 16% by epoch 30 while training loss kept falling, which is the classic signature of overfitting.
BASE_GAP_SENTENCE: The gap between training and validation accuracy widened from -4.94 pp after the first epoch to 17.01 pp by epoch 30 (62.77% versus 45.76%).
BASE_STABILITY_SENTENCE: After the first five epochs, validation accuracy moved by a typical ±0.98 pp from one epoch to the next, and its largest single-epoch drop was 1.66 pp, so optimization itself was stable; the problem with the baseline is generalization, not stability.
BS_RANK_SENTENCE: Ranked by best validation accuracy, batch size 512 came first (49.78%), followed by 128 (48.68%) and 32 (46.94%).
BS_SPREAD_SENTENCE: The gap between the best and worst setting was 2.84 pp, a difference that clears both the 1-pp noise band and a paired McNemar test (p < 0.001), so batch size did make a measurable difference here.
BS_EPOCH_SENTENCE: Counted in epochs, validation accuracy peaked at epoch 15 (batch 32), 21 (batch 128) and 30 (batch 512); counted in weight updates, those peaks came after roughly 21,105, 7,392 and 2,640 updates. Small batches reached their best point in fewer epochs only by taking many more steps; per update, the large batch made more progress, because each of its steps averages over 16 times as many images.
BS_LOSS_SENTENCE: The lowest validation loss was 1.543 for batch 32 (epoch 8), 1.494 for batch 128 (epoch 11) and 1.452 for batch 512 (epoch 19). By epoch 30 validation loss had risen above those minima by 20%, 16% and 2% respectively, so batch 32 overfit most strongly within the fixed epoch budget.
BS_TIME_SENTENCE: Training took 176 s at batch 32, 54 s at batch 128 and 22 s at batch 512 on this hardware (NVIDIA L4), so batch 32 was about 8.1 times slower than batch 512 for the same 30 epochs.
BS_STABILITY_SENTENCE: Epoch-to-epoch jitter in validation accuracy (after epoch 5) was 0.75 pp at batch 32, 0.98 pp at 128 and 0.73 pp at 512, so the noisiest curve came from batch 128 and jitter did not simply track batch size in this run.
BS_SELECT_SENTENCE: I carry batch size 512 forward. It had the highest best validation accuracy, and no faster setting came within the noise band of it.
BN_ACC_SENTENCE: With batch normalization, best validation accuracy went from 49.78% to 40.64% (-9.14 pp), a difference that clears both the 1-pp noise band and a paired McNemar test (p < 0.001).
BN_LOSS_SENTENCE: The lowest validation loss was 1.700 with batch normalization (epoch 3) against 1.452 without it (epoch 19).
BN_SPEED_SENTENCE: The batch-normalized network never reached the 47.3% target, while the plain network did so in epoch 8. After a single epoch, validation accuracy was 28.30% with batch normalization and 34.72% without.
BN_STABILITY_SENTENCE: Validation-accuracy jitter after epoch 5 was 3.04 pp with batch normalization and 0.73 pp without, and the largest single-epoch drops were 8.04 pp and 0.96 pp, so batch normalization made the validation curve noisier.
BN_GAP_SENTENCE: By epoch 30, the train–validation accuracy gap was 55.68 pp with batch normalization and 11.04 pp without, so the normalized network memorized the training set even more aggressively.
BN_TIME_SENTENCE: Batch normalization changed the median epoch time by a factor of 1.17 (0.76 s versus 0.65 s), a modest overhead for the extra normalization work.
BN_VERDICT_SENTENCE: Taken together, batch normalization did not speed up convergence, did not make training more stable, and reduced the best validation accuracy.
EXT_SENTENCE: At a learning rate of 0.005, the plain network's best validation accuracy was 47.60% (status: ok, jitter ±0.76 pp) and the batch-normalized network's was 43.08% (status: unstable, jitter ±3.64 pp), changes of -2.18 pp and +2.44 pp relative to the default learning rate. This fits the claim: moving to the larger step size was far worse for the plain network than for the normalized one.
RS_BEST_SENTENCE: The best random-search configuration was trial 8: 2 hidden layers of 256 units, with batch normalization, dropout 0.4, learning rate 0.005 and batch size 32, which reached 51.06% validation accuracy at epoch 23.
RS_SPREAD_SENTENCE: Across the eight trials, best validation accuracy ranged from 40.76% to 51.06% (median 46.50%), and 8 of the eight beat the Step 4 batch-normalized reference of 40.64%.
RS_EFFECT_SENTENCE: Grouping the trials by each hyperparameter, the spread in mean best validation accuracy was largest for learning rate (7.22 pp between its best value, 0.0001, and its worst, 0.001), followed by dropout (7.21 pp) and batch size (5.71 pp); hidden layers mattered least (2.75 pp).
RS_UNSTABLE_SENTENCE: Of the 8 random-search trials, 4 were flagged: trial 1 (unstable; learning rate 0.005, batch size 256, dropout 0.2, best 46.74%); trial 4 (unstable; learning rate 0.001, batch size 128, dropout 0, best 40.76%); trial 6 (unstable; learning rate 0.0005, batch size 128, dropout 0.2, best 46.26%); trial 8 (unstable; learning rate 0.005, batch size 32, dropout 0.4, best 51.06%).
RS_WEAK_SENTENCE: The weakest trial (#4: 3 hidden layers of 128 units, with batch normalization, dropout 0, learning rate 0.001 and batch size 128) reached only 40.76%; its key observation was: peaked early (epoch 5); noisy validation curve (±2.2 pp per epoch); large train–val gap (19 pp).
BO_BEST_SENTENCE: The best Bayesian trial was #2 (random warm-up): 4 hidden layers of 256 units, with batch normalization, dropout 0.4, learning rate 0.0001 and batch size 32, reaching 53.14% at epoch 27.
BO_PHASE_SENTENCE: The 5 TPE-guided trials averaged 48.04% against 46.50% for the 3 random warm-up trials, and 0 of them beat the best warm-up trial, so with this little data the surrogate was not yet reliably steering toward better regions.
BO_UNSTABLE_SENTENCE: No Bayesian trial failed or met the instability criteria, although trial 5 (learning rate 0.005, batch size 32) had the noisiest validation curve (±1.91 pp per epoch).
BO_REPEAT_SENTENCE: TPE never proposed the same configuration twice.
CMP_ACC_SENTENCE: Bayesian optimization's best trial reached 53.14% against 51.06% for random search (+2.08 pp), a difference that clears both the 1-pp noise band and a paired McNemar test (p < 0.001).
CMP_TRIALS_SENTENCE: Taking a strong configuration to mean one within the 1-pp noise band of the best score found by either method (53.14%), random search never got there within its eight trials, and Bayesian optimization first got there in trial 2.
CMP_STABILITY_SENTENCE: Trial scores had a standard deviation of 3.34 pp under random search and 4.14 pp under Bayesian optimization. Random search had 0 failed and 4 unstable trials; Bayesian optimization had 0 and 0.
CMP_COMPUTE_SENTENCE: Random search used 10.0 minutes and 164 training epochs in total; Bayesian optimization used 19.1 minutes and 190 epochs. TPE's own overhead for proposing a trial is milliseconds, negligible next to training, so the difference comes almost entirely from which configurations each method chose and how soon early stopping ended them; for example, the mean batch size was 132 for random search and 112 for TPE, and smaller batches cost more time per epoch.
CMP_VERDICT_SENTENCE: Bayesian optimization found the stronger configuration under the same budget (2.08 pp ahead, p < 0.001), although a single seed per trial means this ranking could still shift on a rerun.
FINAL_CONFIG_SENTENCE: The selected model is `bayes_t2` from Step 6: 4 hidden layers of 256 units, with batch normalization, dropout 0.4, learning rate 0.0001 and batch size 32, with the weights taken from epoch 27 of the 30 epochs it trained for.
FINAL_SELECTION_SENTENCE: The top validation score overall was 53.14% (`bayes_t2`). 1 run lay within the noise band of it and 1 of them was stable; the preference for the fewest parameters picked the top-scoring run itself (989,706 parameters).
FINAL_GAP_SENTENCE: Test accuracy (53.05%) was 0.09 pp below the best validation accuracy (53.14%). A small drop is expected: the validation score was used to choose both the configuration and the epoch, so it is optimistically biased, while the test score is not.
FINAL_CLASS_SENTENCE: Per-class test accuracy ranged from 31.40% for dog to 69.60% for ship.
FINAL_CONFUSED_SENTENCE: The most frequent confusions were dog predicted as cat (327 images), automobile predicted as truck (196 images) and bird predicted as deer (161 images).
FINAL_CALIB_SENTENCE: The expected calibration error was 0.015. On average the model was underconfident by 1.20 pp (mean confidence 51.85% against accuracy 53.05%).
SUMMARY_GAIN_SENTENCE: From the baseline's 48.68% to the final model's 53.14%, tuning changed best validation accuracy by +4.46 pp, a difference that clears both the 1-pp noise band and a paired McNemar test (p < 0.001).
SUMMARY_LEVER_SENTENCE: Of the individual stages, searching the full space (dropout, depth, width, learning rate) produced the largest single step (+12.50 pp); the steps were +1.10 pp for choosing the batch size, -9.14 pp for adding batch normalization and +12.50 pp for searching the full space (dropout, depth, width, learning rate).
SUMMARY_PEAK_SENTENCE: In 5 of the 6 fixed 30-epoch runs, validation accuracy peaked at least three epochs before training ended, and keeping the best-epoch weights instead of the last-epoch weights was worth +2.30 pp on average.
SUMMARY_RANGE_SENTENCE: Across all 22 runs that did not fail, best validation accuracy spanned only 40.64% to 53.14%.
SEED_SENTENCE: Retraining the final configuration with seeds 7, 2024 and 31337 gave best validation accuracies of 51.80%, 51.76% and 51.80%. Together with the original run, the mean is 52.13% with a standard deviation of 0.68 pp, which is smaller than the 1-pp noise band. The original run ranked first of the four, a small illustration of the winner's curse: the configuration was selected partly on a favourable first seed.
REC_CONFIG_SENTENCE: Within this search space, the evidence supports 4 hidden layers of 256 units, with batch normalization, dropout 0.4, learning rate 0.0001 and batch size 32 as a sound default, and across all sixteen search trials dropout was the hyperparameter with the widest spread in mean validation accuracy, so it is the first one I would tune more finely.
